pointers.sentence: `ChoiceField.choices` is a property whose setter passes the value through `normalize_choices`, which makes a mapping, an enumeration or nested groups into lists of pairs and wraps a callable to be called at each reading ([Choices: `normalize_choices` and the choice iterators](../utils/choices.md)), and hands the result to the widget's `ChoiceWidget.choices`, which normalizes it again (`django/forms/fields.py:ChoiceField.choices`).
`ChoiceField.__deepcopy__` adds a deep copy of the choices, and the widget copies its own shallowly (`django/forms/widgets.py:ChoiceWidget.__deepcopy__`).

`FilePathField` makes its own choices: the files or directories under its directory that match its pattern, the blank choice first when the field is not required (`django/forms/fields.py:FilePathField.set_choices`).

`ChoiceField.validate` makes the required check of `django/forms/fields.py:Field`, then asks `ChoiceField.valid_value`, which looks through the choices, and inside each group (a pair whose second element is a list or a tuple), for a value equal to the one given or with the same string, which lets a browser's string match a number among the choices.
Anything else is an `"invalid_choice"` error naming the value (`django/forms/fields.py:ChoiceField.validate`, `django/forms/fields.py:ChoiceField.valid_value`).
Anything else is an `"invalid_choice"` error naming the value (`django/forms/fields.py:ChoiceField.validate`, `django/forms/fields.py:ChoiceField.valid_value`).

After the whole of `Field.clean`, `TypedChoiceField._coerce` passes the checked string to the field's `coerce`, and gives `empty_value`, `""` unless another is given, for an empty one; a failed conversion is an `"invalid_choice"` error too (`django/forms/fields.py:TypedChoiceField._coerce`).

`MultipleChoiceField` takes a list: `MultipleChoiceField.to_python` makes an empty value `[]` and each item of a list or a tuple a string, and refuses anything else as `"invalid_list"`; its `validate` checks each distinct item with `valid_value`, and `MultipleChoiceField.has_changed` compares lengths, then sets of strings (`django/forms/fields.py:MultipleChoiceField`).

`ChoiceWidget.get_context` adds the list `ChoiceWidget.optgroups` makes, a triple for each top-level choice: its group's name (`None` outside a group), its options, and its index (`django/forms/widgets.py:ChoiceWidget.optgroups`).

Its index is its place, or its group's and its own joined, `"0_1"` for Berth 2, and `ChoiceWidget.id_for_label` numbers an `"id"` among its attributes with that index (`django/forms/widgets.py:ChoiceWidget.create_option`).

A widget of one value marks only the first match; one whose `ChoiceWidget.allow_multiple_selected` is true marks every match, and reads the data with `MultiValueDict.getlist` where it can, so that a `QueryDict` gives every value submitted under the name (`django/forms/widgets.py:ChoiceWidget.value_from_datadict`).

On a required field, `Select.use_required_attribute` withholds `"required"` from a select of one value whose first choice has a value, which its docstring calls invalid HTML (`django/forms/widgets.py:Select.use_required_attribute`).

A `RadioSelect` puts it on each input, and gives its field's label no `"for"`, for screen readers, its docstring says, and because clicking such a label would toggle the first input (`django/forms/widgets.py:RadioSelect.id_for_label`).
`ModelChoiceField` keeps a queryset in place of a list (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField`).

Assigning `ModelChoiceField.queryset` stores the queryset's `QuerySet.all`, a copy with nothing cached, and hands the widget the field's choices (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField._set_queryset`).

Reading `ModelChoiceField.choices`, unless choices were assigned by hand, makes a new `ModelChoiceIterator`, so that, a comment says, it has not been consumed (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField._get_choices`).

`ModelChoiceIterator` yields the blank choice, `""` with `ModelChoiceField.empty_label`, unless that is `None`; then, for each object, a pair: a `ModelChoiceIteratorValue`, which holds the object's key and the object and is equal to the key, and the label `ModelChoiceField.label_from_instance` gives, the object's `str` by default (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceIterator`).
A select of one value with no blank choice sends two, the first from `Select.use_required_attribute` reading the first choice (`django/forms/widgets.py:Select.use_required_attribute`).
Otherwise it is the label given, `None` again meaning none, and the default, `""`, is replaced by what `get_blank_choice_label` gives (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField.__init__`).
Without it, each form's widget would read the class's field (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField.__deepcopy__`).

`ModelChoiceField.to_python` makes an empty value `None`, refuses a null character, and otherwise fetches the object with `QuerySet.get` on the field's queryset, one query, by `ModelChoiceField.to_field_name` or the primary key; an object of the model is taken by its key (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField.to_python`).
The query is the check against the choices, and `ModelChoiceField.validate` skips `ChoiceField.validate`, keeping only the required check (`django/forms/models.py:ModelChoiceField.validate`).

`ModelMultipleChoiceField.clean` returns `QuerySet.none` for an empty value when not required, and `ModelMultipleChoiceField._check_values` drops repeated keys, builds an unrun filter for each, so that a key of the wrong type is `"invalid_pk_value"`, fetches them all in one query with `"__in"`, and refuses a key it did not find as `"invalid_choice"` (`django/forms/models.py:ModelMultipleChoiceField._check_values`).

`apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield` makes a dictionary a `Q`, adds the condition that the key equal the outer row's, and filters the field's queryset on `Exists` over the model's base manager, which a comment says avoids duplicates (`django/forms/models.py:apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield`).

`ModelFormMetaclass` has `fields_for_model` skip this, and `BaseModelForm.__init__` does it for every field of each instance, so a callable is called for each form (`django/forms/models.py:BaseModelForm.__init__`).

`get_blank_choice_label` gives a blank choice's label: `BLANK_CHOICE_LABEL`, a translated `"- Select an option -"`, or, while `USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` is true, the dashes of `BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` (`django/db/models/utils.py:get_blank_choice_label`).
Its callers include `ModelChoiceField.__init__` and a model field's `get_choices` (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.get_choices`).
